# pulse_allowlist_entry (Resource)

A network that Pulse never bans, e.g. your home or office address. Adding it also lifts active bans inside it. Loopback and private ranges are never banned anyway and need no entry. Import with the network in the form Pulse stores it (a CIDR such as `198.51.100.7/32`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pulse_allowlist_entry" "home" {
  network = "198.51.100.7"
  note    = "Home connection"
}

resource "pulse_allowlist_entry" "office_v6" {
  network = "2001:db8:1200::/48"
  note    = "Office IPv6"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network` (String) IP address or CIDR (IPv4 or IPv6). Spellings of the same network (e.g. `192.0.2.1` and `192.0.2.1/32`) are treated as the same network. Changing the network forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `note` (String) Why the network is allowlisted (at most 256 characters).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The network as Pulse stores it: a CIDR with the host bits cleared; a single IPv4 address becomes `/32` and a single IPv6 address `/128`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the network as Pulse stores it (a bare address is also accepted).
terraform import pulse_allowlist_entry.home 198.51.100.7/32
```
